Operation

Recombination filtering

Identify and remove variation introduced by recombination so the remaining signal reflects vertical descent.

Inputs

  • Whole-genome alignment

Outputs

  • Recombination-filtered alignment
  • Recombinant region coordinates

Recombination imports blocks of sequence from other lineages, producing clusters of variation that violate the single-tree assumption of most phylogenetic methods. Filtering removes those blocks before trees or distances are calculated.

Choosing a method 2

Each method below says when to use it and when another method fits better.

  • Clonal frame inference

    Model recombination along a fixed tree with a hidden Markov model and infer the clonal genealogy.

    Use when

    • You need estimates of recombination parameters, such as the rate of recombination relative to mutation.
    • A tree for the samples already exists from an earlier step.

    Use another method when

    • No tree exists yet, or you want filtering and a tree from a single step. Use Iterative recombination detection instead.

    ClonalFrameML

  • Iterative recombination detection

    Alternate between tree building and detecting regions of elevated SNP density until the result converges.

    Use when

    • Samples are closely related, such as a single lineage or outbreak sharing a recent common ancestor.
    • You want a recombination-filtered alignment and a starting tree in one step.
    • No tree exists yet for your samples.

    Use another method when

    • You need estimates of recombination parameters, such as the relative effect of recombination and mutation. Use Clonal frame inference instead.
    • The collection spans many distantly related lineages, where run time grows and detection becomes less reliable.

    Gubbins
